item.title: 'Disappointment sets in' - Gian Piero Gasperini explains why Roma collapse against Man Utd was WORSE than Real Madrid failure
item.description: FBL-EUR-C1-MAN UTD-ROMA - AFP Gian Piero Gasperini has admitted that Roma’s latest Champions League collapse against Manchester United has left a bitter taste, insisting the defeat offers a harsher lesson than their previous failure against Real Madrid. The Giallorossi threw away a two-goal lead at Old Trafford, echoing a worrying trend of mental fragility that has plagued their European campaign. Old Trafford advantage blown The Italian side appeared in total control early on, racing into a 2-0 lead inside 18 minutes through Matias Soule and a Donyell Malen penalty. Roma created several opportunities to extend their advantage but ultimately failed to capitalise. The match shifted dramatically when Bruno Fernandes converted a retaken penalty. That lifeline sparked a fierce comeback from the hosts, who had not won a match since September 10. Matheus Cunha emerged as the late hero for United, netting a decisive brace to secure a dramatic 3-2 victory. Gasperini dissects Roma capitulation Speaking to Sky Sport Italia , Gasperini highlighted how the momentum shifted drastically after the Fernandes spot-kick. "It was a different game to Real Madrid, where it all happened in the last seven or eight minutes from corner kicks, and there were no real signs of the comeback," he explained. "This time, after the penalty, Manchester United had this sudden surge of enthusiasm, and we were unable to keep up with it." The Italian tactician acknowledged a concerning pattern in his team's ability to hold onto leads. "I don’t think it’s a coincidence, but I also think they were different matches," he added. "This evening, we didn’t have the strength to press their strikers the way we did in the first half, plus the penalty and the error for the equaliser really turned the tide. "There is always going to be 15-20 minutes against Manchester United when you’re under pressure, and if you can emerge unscathed from it, you’ll be fine." A harsh European lesson Reflecting on their tactical shortcomings in the second half, Gasperini felt the Old Trafford collapse provided a more valuable learning curve than their late capitulation against Real Madrid. "Honestly, we learned more from this match than the one with Real Madrid. That felt unpredictable, whereas at times today when Old Trafford was pushing on the team, we need to be able to handle these situations better in future," he conceded. Discussing the tactical shifts, Gasperini pointed out his side's failure to adapt to United's intense pressing. He continued: "They made modifications at half-time and had nothing left to lose, so they pressed high, so perhaps we should’ve made more of long balls in that situation. "The problem was we were no longer able to stick to their reference points, so they had the better on pressing, not letting us play, but also on their attacks. "That created some problems for us, we probably should’ve tried to interrupt their rhythm a bit more with some extra challenges and slow the tempo down.

item.title: Iowa’s Kirk Ferentz shades ESPN for bias before first CFP rankings reveal
item.description: Jeffrey Becker-Imagn Images Iowa’s Kirk Ferentz shades ESPN for bias before first CFP rankings reveal appeared first on ClutchPoints . ESPN is getting a heaping pile of blame for the SEC-heavy presence in the College Football Playoff rankings , but Kirk Ferentz started the bashing early. Before the CFP selection committee unveiled its top-25 for the first time this season, the longtime Iowa head coach fired some shots at the Worldwide Leader in Sports. He was dripping in sarcasm while speaking to the media on Tuesday afternoon. “It’s great for TV, right?” Ferentz joked, per the Hawkeye Historian X account. “ESPN’s loving it. Next time I look at my iPad I’m sure I’ll be reading all about it and can’t wait. I did notice they seem to promote the sports that they carry. Is that correct? I’m figuring that out.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The two-time Big Ten champion did not limit his ESPN-based criticism to just college football. He turned his attention to America’s Pastime before circling back to the gridiron. “You couldn’t find anything on the World Series, until the last game. I’m living in the same world, right? I’m like ‘are they still playing the World Series or what? Oh yeah, Fox {and} ESPN’ We’re not {on} ESPN, so we probably won’t make the rankings. Haven’t gone that far, but anyway, I’m not too worried about it.” An all-time KF press conference tangent today about tv networks pic.twitter.com/bI7VqhRCNx — Hawkeye Historian (@Hawk_Historian) November 3, 2026 Ferentz took the press room on a wild ride and raised multiple talking points that many fans have been expressing on social media for years. Ultimately, Iowa came in at No. 19. The Hawkeyes stunned Michigan in The Big House and just blanked Wisconsin in Kinnick Stadium, but a blowout loss to Ohio State and a weak non-conference slate puts them in a tough spot. There are currently no more ranked teams on Iowa’s schedule — at Northwestern, versus Purdue, at Illinois and versus Nebraska — so the program would need loads of help. A surprise appearance in the Big Ten championship game is the Hawkeyes’ only plausible path to the 12-team CFP. Nevertheless, Kirk Ferentz just boosted his popularity among many fans by going after the network that televises SEC games. It sounds like he did not tune into ESPN’s College Football Playoff rankings show, and unfortunately for him and his squad, there may not be any reason for him to do so until 2027. item.title: Fifa president Gianni Infantino under fresh spotlight over Trump connections
item.description: Following the Democratic victory in the midterm elections, Fifa president Gianni Infantino could be compelled to answer questions about his relationship with United States President Donald Trump under threat of criminal penalties. An inquiry was formally launched by Democrats on the House Judiciary Committee on July 26, targeting what was described as a "sustained campaign" by Infantino and global football's governing body to win favour with President Trump. The panel asked Infantino to provide relevant documents and give testimony. A spokeswoman for the committee’s Democrats revealed on September 23 that the level of co-operation provided by Fifa and its leadership had been "woefully inadequate". While the party previously lacked the authority to issue subpoenas carrying criminal consequences as the minority, their midterm success grants them the leverage to force compliance and subject Infantino to heightened scrutiny. The committee spokeswoman stated that although staff received a briefing regarding litigation connected to the Fifa bribery scandal, "Fifa has yet to turn over any priority documents requested by the committee – including those that would show how much money Fifa has given the Trump family – answer key questions around the awarding of the Fifa Peace Prize or explain how the Kushner-Infantino scheme to sell off the World Cup was conceived." Infantino was also embroiled in controversy at the World Cup after USMNT player Folarin Balogun had a red card overturned (Getty) Two days after the congressional inquiry began, on July 28, The Times disclosed that Infantino was shaping a strategy to sell stakes in Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) to private investors. Fifa subsequently confirmed the enterprise would handle commercial operations for the World Cup and other tournaments, with the primary investor group led by Thrive Capital—a firm established by Joshua Kushner, the brother of President Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner . The FFE proposal was abandoned on August 1 after being rejected by three continental confederations, including UEFA , which threatened a tournament boycott. Uefa stated it had "lost confidence" in Infantino over the incident and pledged to field an opposing candidate for the forthcoming Fifa presidential election, though no challenger has been named with two weeks remaining before the nomination deadline. While Infantino appears to retain solid support across Africa, Asia, Oceania and South America, campaign group FairSquare has urged national associations to contest his eligibility for a fourth term. Fifa statutes cap presidential tenures at three terms, the Fifa Council ruled on the eve of the 2022 World Cup final to discount Infantino’s initial period between 2016 and 2019, leaving him eligible to run again in 2027.

item.title: Skoda to reconsider ice hockey worlds sponsorship if Russia plays
item.description: ILLUSTRATION - A Skoda emblem is seen on a car's hood during the second day of the 89th Geneva Motor Show. (is associated with: «Skoda to reconsider ice hockey worlds sponsorship if Russia plays») Uli Deck/dpa Carmaker Skoda plans to reconsider its sponsorship of the 2027 ice hockey world championships in Germany if Russia is allowed to participate in the tournament. A spokeswoman for the Czech company told the CTK news agency that Russia's return would be incompatible with the values upheld by Skoda due to Moscow's war in Ukraine. If that were to happen, Skoda would have to reconsider its participation in the world championships and take further steps. Skoda is the main sponsor of the tournament. Russia were permitted to compete by the Court of Arbitration for Sport after the International Ice Hockey Federation had already decided to continue to exclude Russian teams for this season, citing security concerns. While Germany is discussing whether to hand back its hosting rights, several nations, among them world champions Finland, are threatening to boycott the event.

item.title: Mark Pope is giving the BBN exactly what they wanted
item.description: Since taking the helm of the Kentucky Basketball program, Mark Pope has largely been seen as a deeply analytical, measured head coach. The former med school student talks about controlling what you can control and letting go of the rest. While few question his on-court coaching, one of Big Blue Nation’s biggest criticisms was that he could sometimes seem a little too calculated on the sidelines. Fans wanted to see raw emotion. They wanted fire. Pope appears to have taken that feedback and ran with it. The transformation began during the offseason. Pope arrived at summer workouts with a rugged beard, and he later went viral with a swagger-filled video set to the 50 Cent track “Many Men.” Mark Pope with “Many Men” to close the video. Cold. 🥶 “Many men, wish death upon me.” https://t.co/MAophcdCMf pic.twitter.com/mdF9Ve56tR — Tristan Pharis (@TristanUda) May 8, 2026 Almost instantly, the Kentucky fanbase embraced this new attitude and affectionately labeled it the “Dark Pope” era. If anyone thought the offseason persona was just for social media, Tuesday night’s season-opening victory over Manhattan proved otherwise. Late in the game, despite the Wildcats’ commanding 31-point lead, Pope erupted on the sideline. Dissatisfied with a lapse in execution, he was seen visibly berating his team during a timeout. Just prior to that, he had snapped a whiteboard over his knee. It was exactly the kind of relentless standard and fiery passion fans have been begging to see. Mark Pope broke a whiteboard over his knee and has been letting Kentucky hear about it. pic.twitter.com/idADO1s8G5 — Rare Rookies (@rarerookies) November 4, 2026 However, Pope knows he has to manage these explosive moments strategically. Addressing his sideline demeanor last season, he explained that he has to be careful when he goes white-hot. If a coach operates at a level 10 all the time, the players become numb to it, and the emotion completely loses its meaning. By saving that level of intensity for moments when the team’s standard drops, even in a blowout, Pope sends a clear message to his locker room. The fans who wanted a more fiery leader have officially gotten their wish, and the Dark Pope era seems to be here to stay.

item.title: Ravens vs. Jaguars: Statistical breakdown, key matchups for Week 9
item.description: The Baltimore Ravens are preparing for Thursday Night Football against the Jacksonville Jaguars , and the statistical comparison reveals just how difficult their Week 9 assignment could become. Jacksonville enters the matchup at 5-2, averaging 28 points per game while allowing just 15.9, the NFL's second-best scoring defense. Baltimore, meanwhile, has fallen to 4-4 following three consecutive losses and will turn to undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano for his first NFL start. The Ravens average 22.4 points and 338.6 total yards per game, ranking 19th and 15th, respectively. Jacksonville ranks fifth in scoring and 10th in total offense, averaging 350.3 yards per contest. However, the most intriguing numbers involve two areas that could determine whether Baltimore can remain competitive: Jacksonville's dominant rushing defense and its vulnerable pass coverage. Derrick Henry faces the NFL's top-ranked rushing defense The Ravens rank sixth in rushing offense, averaging 133.5 yards per game, but they'll face a Jaguars defense allowing an NFL-low 77.4 rushing yards per contest. That creates a significant challenge for offensive coordinator Declan Doyle, who must establish Derrick Henry without placing excessive responsibility on Fagnano. Jacksonville's interior defense could look different Thursday after starting defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton suffered a season-ending injury against Indianapolis. Losing Hamilton, one of the Jaguars' most important interior defenders, could create opportunities for Baltimore to move the ball up the middle. Henry rushed for 53 yards and a touchdown on 11 carries against Buffalo. The Ravens will likely need a more consistent rushing attack to keep Fagnano out of obvious passing situations. Joe Fagnano faces a vulnerable Jaguars pass defense Jacksonville's defensive statistics reveal an interesting contrast. Despite ranking second in scoring defense, the Jaguars allow 253.9 passing yards per game, 29th in the NFL. Baltimore has opportunities to exploit that weakness, but the challenge is doing so with an inexperienced quarterback who completed 10 of 21 passes for 91 yards with an interception and a lost fumble in Sunday's 36-10 loss to Buffalo. Doyle must balance attacking Jacksonville's secondary with protecting Fagnano, who is also managing an ankle injury. Quick passes, play-action and designed touches for Zay Flowers could help create manageable opportunities without requiring the rookie to consistently challenge Jacksonville downfield. The Jaguars also lost starting safety Eric Murray to a season-ending injury, creating another potential adjustment in their defensive coverage. Jacksonville holds significant scoring and third-down advantages The biggest statistical difference between these teams is scoring efficiency. Jacksonville averages 28 points per game compared with Baltimore's 22.4, while allowing 9.5 fewer points per contest. The Jaguars also convert 48.2% of their third-down opportunities, ranking third in the NFL.

item.title: Derby 0-4 Norwich - the fans' verdict
item.description: [BBC] We asked for your thoughts after Norwich City's 4-0 win against Derby County at Pride Park. Here are some of your comments: Derby fans Russ: The blame lies solely at the feet of David Clowes. He's sold Eustace down the river with the shambolic events of the summer. Cornishram: I'm not one for getting rid of a manager, but this has gone too far. I'm sorry Mr Clowes but the time has come. Christopher: We were second best in every department. No fight or urgency from the players. One or two shots on goal in 90 mins very unlikely to win you a game. Dreadful defending again. The fault and blame can't all be the manager. John: Woeful, amateur, abject. Derby are utterly embarrassing, this won't change until the manager does. Adrian: Derby are very poor and disjointed due to the injuries that have decimated any cohesion or confidence built through last season. Early good performances have now disappeared and we now have to aim to avoid relegation but we can't earn a point, never mind a win. I would give Eustace the the rest of season as changing the manager now would not change the situation with the team or the injury list which is getting longer each game. Per: Painful to watch. Schoolboy defending. Midfielders being outplayed. Nobody winning duels. Hardly creating any chances at our home ground. Time for a change, manager and some players must go. Tim: Absolutely appalling display. No obvious gameplan or strategy. Everyone playing for themselves not the team. Second to every free ball. No meaningful tackles at crucial points in the game and dangerous positions on the pitch. Not sharp or match fit. Never seen a Derby team perform as poorly as this. Recent results say it all. We are destined for another spell in League One unless some decisive action is taken. Norwich fans Paul: Excellent from Norwich. Totally controlled the game and Derby were lucky it was only FOUR! Tommyc44: Been a NCFC fan for too long. Seen too many boom and bust cycles of promotion, stagnation and relegation. This doesn't feel like a boom period to me... but a good performance from the lads. I hope they prove me wrong. OTBC. Robert: A good, solid performance, a very worthy three points, and a clean sheet, at last. The players seem to have found their confidence again, and it seems to be clicking together well. That said, we were up against a very poor Derby team. Michael: A really one sided affair. Derby looked destined for the drop. Let's hope this revival for Norwich lasts. They are truly a side with the potential of getting into a play-off position. Roger: At last Norwich displaying some of last season's energy and desire when PC took over. Still a few too many poor passes, but overall everyone contributed to a pleasing win. Every goal was constructed from attacking prowess rather than luck. This performance gives renewed hope. Well done. Rob: Yes a great win and most importantly a clean sheet but it was against a very poor Derby. There will be much bigger tests to come.

item.title: Rwanda's army team removed from Africa league after US sanctions, NBA says
item.description: Rwanda's army team APR came third in the Basketball Africa League last year [Anadolu via Getty Images] The National Basketball Association (NBA) says it removed Rwanda's army team from its African league because of US sanctions imposed on the country in March. The NBA had previously said the Rwandan army-funded Armée Patriotique Rwandaise (APR) club would not participate in the 2026 Basketball Africa League (BAL). However this is the first time the NBA has revealed the reasons behind the APR's removal. The association was responding to complaints by two US senators, who sent a letter asking them to reconsider their partnership with the Rwandan team. The US placed sanctions on the Rwandan army, accusing it of fuelling the conflict in the Democratic Republic of Congo in March. The senators said the NBA risked "becoming complicit in sportswashing by accepting money from a Rwandan government that systematically abuses human rights". Last week, the US also imposed sanctions on Rwanda's defence ministry over its support for the M23 rebel group which has seized control of large parts of eastern DR Congo. Rwanda denies backing the rebels despite overwhelming evidence. Rwanda is an official BAL partner and pays the league to host its finals at the 10,000-seat BK Arena in the capital, Kigali. What is the Basketball Africa League? The evidence that shows Rwanda is backing rebels in DR Congo In the letter to the NBA dated 23 October, Democratic Senator Jeffrey Merkley and Republican counterpart Marsha Blackburn gave the association until 2 November to give a written response regarding its continued partnership with Rwanda. "What is the NBA red line for accepting money from foreign governments that commit human rights abuses?" the senators asked. Among other queries, they also questioned how the association could "reconcile its continued partnership with Rwanda with its purported commitment to justice". In its response, NBA deputy commissioner Mark Tatum said the Rwandan team "had been withdrawn" from the BAL following the sanctions imposed earlier in the year, American sports website ESPN reports. The NBA said the APR basketball club would remain barred while the US sanctions are in place. The APR is one of Rwanda's top basketball teams and represented the country in the BAL in 2024 and 2025, when it came third. It was replaced by the RSSB Tigers this year. The BAL is a pan-African basketball league established and co-organised by the NBA and the basketball's world governing body Fiba. It is a professional league featuring 12 club teams from across the continent. Rwanda has hosted all but one of the league's final and playoff matches since the inaugural match in 2021. The NBA reportedly receives millions of dollars annually from the country for the marketing and partnership rights. item.title: Lyon coach Fonseca follows his heart to Sporting Lisbon
item.description: Lyon's Portuguese head coach Paulo Fonseca has joined Sporting Lisbon (Sameer AL-DOUMY) French club Lyon confirmed on Wednesday the departure of Portuguese coach Paulo Fonseca to Sporting Lisbon with a compensation fee of five million euros ($5.6 mn) paid to the Ligue 1 side. Fonseca, 53, joined Lyon in January 2025 as a replacement for Pierre Sage and had been under contract until the end of this season. "Paulo came to see me last week to say that he had received an offer from Sporting and had accepted it, explaining that it was a choice of the heart as it is his boyhood club," Lyon sporting director Matthieu Louis-Jean told AFP. "I wasn't expecting this at all. I tried to understand his reasons, but it quickly became clear that, for him, it was an offer he couldn't refuse and for us, it would be difficult, because you can't keep someone against their will." The former Porto, Shakhtar Donetsk, Lille and AC Milan coach guided Lyon to a fourth-place finish last term, but they missed out on this season's Champions League league phase after losing in the play-offs. Fonseca's spell at Lyon came during a turbulent financial period. In June 2025, French football's financial watchdog provisionally relegated the club to Ligue 2 before the decision was overturned on appeal, subject to a strict programme of cost-cutting measures and player sales. The club also stuck by Fonseca after he was given a nine-month domestic ban last year for an angry altercation with a referee. While thanking Fonseca for his commitment, Lyon expressed "deep regret" regarding what they described as an "unexpected decision" mid-season with the club third in Ligue 1. Lyon are expected to appoint a permanent successor during the upcoming international break, with former Braga coach Carlos Vicens reportedly among the leading candidates. Assistant Jorge Maciel will take charge of Lyon on an interim basis for the club's next two matches, Thursday's Europa League fixture against Real Sociedad and Sunday's Ligue 1 trip to Brest. fjt/mla/ea/mw

item.title: Barcelona injury update: Versatile star set to return vs Atletico Madrid but defender still a doubt
item.description: Barcelona injury update: Versatile star set to return vs Atletico Madrid but defender still a doubt Barcelona are set to welcome Eric Garcia back for Sunday’s La Liga meeting with Atletico Madrid, with the defender progressing well after recovering from a muscle injury. According to Carlos Monfort , the Spaniard has resumed training with the squad and is increasingly confident after spending several days working with the ball. As such, barring an unexpected setback, he should be available to Hansi Flick. On the other hand, the situation is less encouraging for Jules Kounde, who has yet to return to group training. Andreas Christensen, meanwhile, is expected to resume normal training, giving Barcelona another defensive option ahead of their trip to the Metropolitano. Eric Garcia nears Barcelona return after muscle injury Garcia has been recovering from the muscle injury he sustained against Real Betis on October 17. Eric Garcia will be available to face Atletico Madrid. (Photo by Fran Santiago/Getty Images) Barcelona initially estimated that he would require three to four weeks to recover , making the Atletico fixture a realistic target for his comeback. His progress has now reached an important stage, with the defender training alongside his teammates and gradually regaining confidence. His expected availability is particularly valuable because Flick has been dealing with several defensive absences. Kounde remains doubtful as Christensen returns Kounde’s situation is considerably less certain, as the French defender has not yet resumed group training, and his chances of travelling to Madrid will depend on whether he can participate in Thursday’s session. If he remains unavailable for collective training, Barcelona could face another selection problem on the right side of their defence. Kounde is still doubtful for Atletico Madrid clash. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) Christensen’s return to normal training provides some relief, although Flick will need to assess his condition before deciding whether he is ready to feature against Atletico. Barcelona defensive injuries make Garcia’s return important Barcelona’s defensive problems have been evident during recent matches, particularly against Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid, when several regular options were unavailable. Garcia’s injury against Betis added to an already difficult situation, with Kounde and Christensen also dealing with fitness problems. The setback involving young defender Xavi Espart, who is expected to miss approximately seven weeks , has further reduced Flick’s options. Having Garcia available would therefore give the manager greater flexibility when selecting his back four, although it remains to be seen whether the Spaniard will be slotted right into the starting XI.

item.title: British teenager Mika Stojsavljevic beats grand slam champion for first WTA Tour win
item.description: British teenager Mika Stojsavljevic beat former grand slam champion Sofia Kenin in Hong Kong for a landmark first main-draw win on the WTA Tour. The 17-year-old lost in the final round of qualifying for the WTA 250 event but was granted a last-minute reprieve when Canadian Leylah Fernandez, who lost in the Tokyo final on Sunday, withdrew from the main draw. Stojsavljevic only found out she was playing an hour before her match but despite her limited preparation time ground out a tough 6-3 4-6 6-4 win in two hours and 19 minutes over American Kenin, who won her only major at the Australian Open in 2020. There were more than 200 places between the highly-rated teen and her opponent. Stojsavljevic, the 2024 junior US Open champion, was delighted as she celebrated her maiden win on the circuit and said: “I think it was a good match. Obviously I was coming in as a lucky loser, I only knew an hour before that I was going to be playing. I kind of just went out and swung today. “We didn’t have much time to prepare. Obviously I know she’s a grand slam champion so it was never going to be an easy match but I believed in myself and it worked out.” 411th-ranked Stojsavljevic raced into a set and 3-0 lead before Kenin fought back, but she maintained her composure to come through in three sets and convert her second match point. She will face Turkey’s Zeynep Sonmez in the second round. Later on Wednesday eighth seed and British No 1 Katie Boulter suffered a straight-sets defeat to Claire Liu. The American triumphed 7-5 6-4 in an hour and 47 minutes to book her place in the third round, where she will play the winner of Stojsavljevic against Sonmez.

item.title: Ohio State's initial CFP ranking is about more than its quarterback
item.description: When Ohio State debuted at No. 12 in this year’s College Football Playoff rankings , putting it just outside the cut line for the bracket, it was easy to assume the loss of starting quarterback Julian Sayin was dragging down the Buckeyes’ ranking. But Hunter Yurachek, the Arkansas athletic director who chairs the selection committee, pointed to other factors for keeping the Buckeyes outside the playoff picture behind three other two-loss teams, including No. 5 Alabama. It was about more than the disruption caused by Sayin’s injury, which led the Buckeyes to start Luke Fahey in last week's 30-18 loss at USC . “The fact that their offense wasn't more efficient against a USC defense that had not been very good to this point in the season was a little bit surprising, but we can't put that all on a freshman quarterback,” Yurachek said on a teleconference on Nov. 3. The committee’s concerns rested with stalled drives in the Trojans ’ territory, as the Buckeyes settled for four field goals inside their 30-yard line and did not score a touchdown until just over 2 minutes left. Four trips to the red zone produced just 12 points. The Buckeyes’ defense was also vulnerable to explosive plays at USC. Wide receiver Trent Mosley took off for a 69-yard touchdown on the second play from scrimmage, and tight end Mark Bowman had a highlight-reel hurdle on a 70-yard catch in the third quarter that set up another touchdown. “We evaluated their defense probably a little bit stronger than we evaluated their offense,” Yurachek said. The CFP’s selection principles give the committee leeway to weigh injuries to key players when comparing similar teams. When unbeaten Florida State was left out of the four-team playoff in 2023, the committee pointed to the loss of quarterback Jordan Travis, who had suffered a season-ending leg injury just over two weeks before Selection Sunday, as a significant factor. But the committee hasn’t adopted a similar stance toward Ohio State as Sayin remains sidelined indefinitely . “We don’t look at them as a different team per se,” Yurachek said. The committee’s restraint is a product of a limited sample size. Yurachek referred to them having just one data point without Sayin, who helped lead the Buckeyes to wins at No. 4 Indiana and No. 19 Iowa in October. Fahey threw for 260 yards and one touchdown without an interception against the Trojans in his first start . Even if Ohio State wasn’t quite as explosive in its downfield passing game with the quarterback change, it hardly fell apart. The Buckeyes managed 464 yards of total offense, more than in previous weeks against Indiana and Maryland. But Fahey will face further scrutiny in November as the Buckeyes move forward . Hartford was the unlucky visitor to Keaney Gymnasium that year, and Holy Cross now sits alongside the Hawks in program record books after this short trip to the Ryan Center. item.title: Zoom Diallo thanks BBN for support in his UK debut: “It brought that joy out that I needed”
item.description: Entering Tuesday night’s matchup against Manhattan, much of the attention surrounding Kentucky Basketball was on guard Zoom Diallo. Before the Wildcats’ season opener, Diallo deactivated his Instagram account, leading many fans to believe he was stepping away from social media because of the criticism and negativity he received during the exhibition games. Diallo had struggled at times during those games, and some fans went beyond constructive criticism by directing personal attacks toward him online. His decision to deactivate Instagram sparked many Kentucky fans to support him, and Diallo eventually reactivated his account to say he was doing fine. On Tuesday night, Diallo showed what he could bring to the Wildcats in his first official game. He finished with 12 points on 4/7 shooting from the field, three rebounds, two assists, and two steals while posting a plus-four +/-. While Diallo was on the floor, Kentucky fans could be heard chanting his name, showing their support for the guard. He certainly took notice of the moment. “It brought that joy out that I needed,” Diallo said after the game. “I appreciate BBN, you know, most definitely for showing the love, man. I see everything, and it makes it better, and I am happy that I am here, and I appreciate you guys. Thank you so much.” Kentucky head coach Mark Pope also made it clear how important Diallo is to the team, emphasizing that his contributions go beyond individual statistics. “Zoom is an integral part of this team. When you sometimes you nitpick individual plays, or individual stats, or individual things, and we are all drawn to that because those are the stories to tell. Zoom is like the great connector of our team.” Pope also compared Diallo’s role on the team to a powerful sermon. The sermon told the story of two friends who ran 100 miles together. After completing 90 miles, one man stopped at a tree, but his friend encouraged him to continue through the final 10 miles together. Just before reaching the finish line, the friend encouraged the other to go ahead and enjoy the moment by himself because he had earned it. Several months later, a picture of the moment revealed something the man had not realized: His friend had been carrying both of their packs throughout the final 10 miles. Pope believes Diallo is doing something similar for this Kentucky team, quietly carrying a significant responsibility while helping those around him succeed. “He is carrying the pack for every guy on this team, and his value will always be more than just the numbers. He is going to continue to grow and have success and be a crucial part of what we are as a team this entire season.” For Diallo, Tuesday night’s performance and the support from Kentucky fans were encouraging signs as he continues to settle into his role in Lexington. item.title: Cibastian Broughton's Akron Zips comeback could create silver lining. Opinion
item.description: Akron 's Cibastian Broughton limped off the field at InfoCision Stadium late in the third quarter. Later, the quarterback nicknamed "Worm" missed two snaps after Ohio nose tackle Nathan Hale spun him around and slammed him to the turf late in the fourth quarter. But Broughton kept returning. In Broughton's first game back from a leg injury, he took a beating and made a crucial mistake during Akron's 28-20 loss to Ohio on Tuesday, Nov. 3. But the combination of Broughton's playmaking ability and toughness also gives the Zips a glimmer of hope as they stare down the barrel of a one-win season. Without Broughton completing a comeback from a five-game absence, Akron (1-8, 0-5 in the Mid-American Conference) would not have put Ohio (7-2, 5-0) on upset alert in front of a national TV audience. During Akron coach Joe Moorhead's postgame news conference, he spotted Broughton enter the back of the makeshift interview room. Moorhead paused to tell Broughton, "Keep your head up. You hear me?" Broughton understood the message. Moorhead and his players were devastated about blowing the 17-14 lead they earned against Ohio with 9:35 left in the fourth quarter of a game televised in prime time by ESPN2. Akron running back Jordan Gant pushed the pile and dragged defenders during a 12-play drive he capped with a 1-yard rushing touchdown. Then Broughton connected with wide receiver Marcel Williams in the end zone, giving the Zips the three-point advantage. But Aidan Stire's ensuing kickoff was fair caught by Ohio at its 40-yard line, giving the Bobcats good field position and setting the stage for their rally. Moorhead explained Akron had hoped to execute a "sky kick" to the Ohio 25, not the 40, while avoiding dynamic Bobcats return man Darren James-Hamilton. The now-former Seminoles head coach will always be linked to the quarterback position. Norvell, who was fired on Sunday, Nov. 1 , after a 36-24 loss to Clemson, had a complicated history with his signal callers. Jordan Travis became an icon of the university under Norvell, and may have well led the team to a national title in 2023 if not for a devastating leg injury. The pair will forever be linked, and Travis posted 8,644 yards and 65 touchdowns while rushing for 1,910 yards and 31 touchdowns during his time in Tallahassee. Travis was a holdover from the Willie Taggart era after transferring from Louisville, and split time as a starter in 2021 with Mckenzie Milton. Travis would go on to establish himself as one of the ACC's premier quarterbacks and helped lead Norvell and the program to the heights it hadn't reached since the days of Jimbo Fisher. Norvell went 29-10 with Travis as his quarterback, which gave him well over half of his total 41 victories as FSU head coach. But outside of Travis, he never found a signal caller capable of executing his vision. Without Travis under center, Norvell went 12-29, and did so with mostly transfer quarterbacks having failed to properly develop a high school signee. Who were Mike Norvell's FSU QBs after Jordan Travis? Portal additions of DJ Uiagalelei, Tommy Castellanos and Ashton Daniels — who is the current starter and has thrown for 1,968 yards, 14 touchdowns and rushed for 12 scores — have all left more to be desired. His prep recruitment at the position never produced a gem, and his highest-rated quarterback, Luke Kromenhoek, only spent one season with the program before entering the transfer portal. Uiagalelei was a high-priced gamble in 2024, and while he was directly responsible for the 2-10 record, his shortcomings were obvious. Both Brock Glenn, now at Western Kentucky, and Kromenhoek, at USF, split starting reps after an injury to Uiagalelei, and neither sparked a turnaround. Glenn left in the transfer portal in 2025, and Kromenhoek transferred to Mississippi State after 2024, before transferring again to USF. Adding to what was a miserable year for the Seminoles was that the program nearly had former Miami quarterback Cam Ward, a Heisman Trophy finalist and the No. 1 overall pick in the NFL draft after his lone season with the Hurricanes. item.title: Tenerife to hold memorial service for De Miguel on Saturday
item.description: People gather at Gate 9 of the stadium during an event organised by Tenerife supporters to pay tribute to the player Jesus de Miguel, at the Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez Stadium. CD Tenerife’s Spanish striker Jesus de Miguel died today as a result of a blow sustained during the match against Andorra from goalkeeper Jesus Owono, which caused him to go into cardiac arrest. (is associated with: «Tenerife to hold memorial service for De Miguel on Saturday») Europa Press Canarias/EUROPA PRESS/dpa Spain's CD Tenerife will hold a memorial service to bid farewell to their late forward Jesús de Miguel on Saturday, the second division club said in a statement. All fans are invited to attend a mass, which will be held at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López stadium. The players, the coaching staff and the club management will also attend De Miguel's funeral in Navahermosa. It's unclear, however, when the funeral will be held. Tenerife majority shareholder Rayco García said that De Miguel's body is to be taken to Navahermosa either later on Wednesday or on Thursday at the latests, at the family's request. The small town in central Spain, the family’s hometown, is located around 130 kilometres from Madrid. The town declared a three-day mourning period. De Miguel is survived by his partner, María, and their daughter, Carla, who was born in June 2025. The 30-year-old player died in hospital on Tuesday following a cardiac arrest having violently collided with an on-rushing goalkeeper during a Spanish second-division match. The incident has caused consternation in Spain because of the ferocity of the challenge from FC Andorra keeper Jesús Owono, who was sent off for the foul near the halfway line, and the fact De Miguel was breathing on his own en route to hospital having been resuscitated.

Preview: Cardiff City and West Ham face off amid Hammers’ managerial uncertainty
item.description: Preview: Cardiff City and West Ham face off amid Hammers’ managerial uncertainty Cardiff City welcome a managerless West Ham after they dismissed their head coach, Nuno Espírito Santo, on Tuesday morning. After back-to-back home defeats to promotion rivals, West Ham have decided to part ways with Nuno, despite his EFL Championship Manager of the Month award last month. West Ham currently sit eighth after 13 games, having been unbeaten in the league for nine matches before their consecutive defeats. In the statement regarding Nuno’s departure, the club confirmed that Mark Noble, Steve Potts and Gerard Prenderville will take temporary charge of the squad ahead of the visit to the Welsh capital. While no official announcement has been made yet, it has been widely reported by the likes of Sky Sports and the BBC that Scott Parker has agreed to become West Ham’s next manager. Parker, out of management since leaving Club Brugge in 2022, is no stranger to the Hammers, having spent four seasons in East London and earning Hammer of the Year three years running. He could be in the dugout for Wednesday night’s fixture, but it seems unlikely given the timeframe. As for the Bluebirds, they sit in eighteenth, only four points above the relegation zone, but have shown an improvement in recent games, especially at home, where they remain unbeaten this season. After three games unbeaten, Cardiff fell 3-0 to promotion chasers Wolverhampton Wanderers on Saturday. Ahead of the clash, Bluebirds boss Brian Barry-Murphy addressed the media, discussing West Ham and providing an injury update. “Any changes that West Ham may or may not make, they still have the same players, who have obvious qualities. We know and respect them, but we don’t fear them. “We’ll check on Krystian [Bielik] in training today; he’s close. I think he has a chance. Rubin [Colwill] obviously was a big positive for us on Saturday, to come back and feel so good after his appearance from the bench. “Isaak Davies has a hamstring injury, so he won’t be fit for four weeks. Perry [Ng] didn’t train yesterday but seems okay. We’re hopeful on him. Alex Robertson and Will Fish both didn’t train yesterday, so we’ll check on them again.” As for the Hammers, they could be without Konstantinos Mavropanos for the second game in a row following the knee injury he sustained against Southampton, but he did feature in training this week. Kyle Walker-Peters is set to miss out after suffering an injury on Saturday, with Joël Veltman in line to take his place. With the departure of Nuno, certain players like Alphonse Areola, Edson Álvarez and Soungoutou Magassa could all be reintroduced to the squad. The match is scheduled to kick off at 7:45pm on Wednesday, November 4, and will be shown live on Sky Sports+ in the UK.
